brief: SC's October outlook frames oil prices (testing USD 100/bbl on the unresolved US-Iran conflict and fears of shipping restrictions spreading to the Bab al-Mandab Strait) as in tension with resilient growth (AI investment, strong PMI and retail sales), and expects growth to win, letting equities focus on earnings strength. SC stays Overweight equities over bonds and cash, preferring US and Asia ex-Japan, because earnings growth (34% in 2026, 16% in 2027) should offset the valuation drag from higher yields. The Fed, ECB and BoJ all hiked in September for the first time together, driven by energy-led inflation; SC expects two more Fed hikes to 4.5% by June 2027, one more ECB hike to 2.75%, and BoJ hikes every quarter to 2% by mid-2027, before cuts from Q3 2027 as inflation fades. SC calls this a 1990s-style healthy hiking cycle, not 2022, so it favors credit over duration (3-7yr) and stays Overweight EM USD bonds. Gold stays Overweight (targets USD 4,750/5,000), while WTI targets are raised to USD 100 (3m) and set at USD 80 (12m). SC's own quant model trimmed its equity Overweight to +1 from +3 on weaker valuation, though it still flags low near-term bear-market odds.
